Item No. 2  – Public Hearing  Submitted by: Kelly Ribuffo, Contract Planner

A Public Hearing considering a Site Plan Review and a Variance to excavate under an existing
single-family residence to create a new 372 square foot family room and bathroom partially below
grade in the Multiple Residential, Medium Density (MD-R) zone. The property is located at 86
Sol Vista (Avalon Terrace Road). The project is categorically exempt from the provisions of the
California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines 15301 (Class 1 –
Existing Facilities). The proposed project is located within the Coastal Zone and is excluded from
Costal Development Permit requirements per Avalon Municipal Code (AMC) Section 9-
8.102.b.1.

Existing Site:

The site is developed with a two-story attached residential condominium within a building with
six total units. The unit also includes an unfinished crawlspace that is accessible via an at-grade
door on the west side of the building. Photos of the existing elevation and crawlspace are included
as Attachment 2.

The Los Angeles County Assessor lists the year built as 1975. The building reflects a vernacular
mid-century architectural style, with design elements including stucco siding, clay tile roof, and
wood balcony railings.

  2
 Existing Area Context:

The project site is located on the south side of the Sol Vista Condominium community. The
community is generally located between Middle Terrace Road to the north and Wrigley Road to
the south and east, and Lower Terrace Road to the west, with primary access via Beacon Street.
The property was approved as a congregate housing development, which is a conditionally
permitted use in the MD-R zoning district. The community consists of 71 homes and
approximately 13 density bonus units and is managed by the Sol Vista Homeowners Association.
Several units within the community have permitted lower-level buildouts, including 87 Sol Vista
located within the same building as the project site. Buildings vary between two and three stories
depending on previous improvements made to each unit and the relationship to adjacent grade.

Properties around Sol Vista Condominiums consist of residential properties also zoned MD-R,
including Canyon Terrace and Bahia Vista Condominiums to the west and single-family residence
along Lower Terrace Road and Middle Terrace Road to the north.

Entitlement and Permit History:

The subject property has no past planning entitlement application history on record.

The property owner has submitted a building permit application at-risk for concurrent review with
the Planning application for this project. No permit for any work related to the proposed project
shall be issued or denied prior to final determination by the Planning Commission.

  PROJECT DESCRIPTION

The project proposes to excavate the crawlspace under the existing residential unit to create a new
372 square foot family room and bathroom partially below grade. The new third story will be
accessed through an internal staircase to the main living level above and by a new entrance at grade
into the courtyard to the west. Proposed plans are included as Attachment 3 to this report.

The proposed project complies with development standards set forth in Avalon Municipal Code
(AMC) Section 9-5.305 for the MD-R zoning district as follows:

The Sol Vista Homeowners Association has reviewed and approved the proposed project, pending

  DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS

Issue 1 – Variance for Three-Story Building:

Per AMC Section 9-5.305.e.1.i, on lots with an average slope of 14° or less, no portion of the
building may exceed a height greater than 28 feet above the lot's natural surface and shall not be
more than two levels. Lots with a steeper grade may increase up to three levels. There is no
definition for “level” in the municipal code, but levels may consist of finished spaces such as
stories, basements, or open decks depending on the configuration of the building or structure.

The existing building the unit is located in meets the overall height requirement and is currently
two stories. The existing crawlspace does not meet the municipal code definitions for a story or
basement (AMC Sections 9-3.602 and 9-3.619) as it is not a space with a floor or ceiling.
According to the project plans, the average slope of grade under the unit is 10°. Construction of
the new lower-level family room and bathroom would result in the unit becoming three stories in
height, which is not permitted based on the average slope of the lot. Therefore, granting of a
Variance is required to allow construction of the new living space as proposed by the applicant.

It is the opinion of staff that a Variance may be granted for the new third story buildout based on
the following considerations:

  •  The proposed project meets all other development standards for a three-level building in
  the MD-R zone, including height and floor area. Therefore, it will comply with existing
  height and massing standards and will remain visually compatible with the surrounding Sol
  Vista Condominium community.

  •  Allowing the applicant to expand their living space within the existing footprint of their
  unit will have minimal impact on the privacy of surrounding properties. It will not decrease

  4
   existing setbacks and the space will be partially below grade, with no windows or decks
  that can look into the private spaces of surrounding residences.

  •  Other units within the greater Sol Vista Condominium community have previously been
  granted approval for lower level, third story buildouts by the City, including 87 Sol Vista
  within the same building. Therefore, approval of the variance would not grant the applicant
  any special privileges inconsistent with existing property development patterns.

Findings and conditions are provided in the staff report and draft resolution to support the granting
of a Variance. In particular, Condition #6 states that no conversion of the family room space to
create a new bedroom shall be permitted without appropriate review by the Planning & Building
Department and provision of a will serve letter from Southern California Edison Company
(“SCE”) that adequate freshwater allocation is available for the proposed conversion.

  GENERAL PLAN, LAND USE, AND ZONING COMPLIANCE

Annual Growth Policy:

The growth policy provides that new residential development would only be permitted with
confirmation from Southern California Edison Company (“SCE”) that adequate fresh water is
available. The project involves an addition to an existing single-family dwelling unit which does
not increase the number of bedrooms in the unit. Therefore, no water allocation is required at the
time. Staff recommends that the Planning Commission make the finding that the proposed project
is in compliance with the 2023 Annual Growth Policy.

Affordable Housing Ordinance:

This ordinance is not applicable to the proposed project since the proposal does not include the
development of five or more residential units.

Site Plan Review:

AMC Chapter 9-8.203 sets forth the required findings for approval of a Site Plan Review as
follows:

  1. Every use, development of land and application of development standards shall take
  place in compliance with all applicable provisions of this title. (AMC Section 9-
  8.203.a)

  With granting of a variance to allow a three-level residential unit, the proposed project
  complies with all applicable development standards as set forth in AMC Section 9-5.305
  for buildings in the Multiple Residential, Medium Density (MD-R) zone, including height
  and maximum floor area.

  2. Every use, development of land and application of development standards shall be
  considered on the basis of the suitability of the site for the particular use or

  5
   development intended, and the total development, including the application of
  prescribed development standards, shall be so arranged as to avoid traffic congestion,
  insure the protection of public health, safety and general welfare, prevent adverse
  effects on neighboring property and shall be in general accord with all elements of the
  General Plan. (AMC Section 9-8.203.b)

  The proposed project meets all other development standards for a three-level building in
  the MD-R zone, including height and floor area. Therefore, it will comply with existing
  height and massing standards and will remain visually compatible with the surrounding Sol
  Vista Condominium community.

  Allowing the applicant to expand their living space within the existing footprint of their
  unit will have minimal impact on the privacy of surrounding properties. It will not decrease
  existing setbacks and the space will be partially below grade, with no windows or decks
  that can look into the private spaces of surrounding residences.

  The use of the property will remain single-family residential, and will create no increased
  traffic or parking demands, nor have any adverse effects on the public health, safety, or
  general welfare of the surrounding community.

  3. Every use, development of land, application of development standards shall be
  considered on the basis of suitable and functional development design, but is not
  intended that such approval be interpreted to require a particular style or type of
  architecture. (AMC Section 9-8.203.c)

  The project site is located in an existing six-unit condominium building and within the
  greater Sol Vista Condominium community. The design elements in the proposed plans
  are consistent with the established design vernacular of the buildings within the community
  and will not stand out as inconsistent with existing development on the site or in the
  vicinity.

Variance:

AMC Chapter 9-8.405 sets forth the required findings for approval of a Variance as follows:

  1. Variances from the terms of the Zoning Ordinance shall be granted only when,
  because of special circumstances applicable to the property including size, shape,
  topography, location or surroundings, the strict application of the Zoning Ordinance
  deprives such property of privileges enjoyed by other property in the vicinity and
  under identical zoning classification.

  The urban fabric of Avalon is relatively compact, with approximately 80-90 acres of
  existing development already located within the valley floor and the immediately
  surrounding hillsides. Individually owned lots in Avalon comprise less than 1% of the total
  city acreage. As such, there is minimal available land for construction of new residential
  units to supply diverse housing options for long-term residents. Therefore, it is important
  to maximize the use of residentially zoned land within the city within the development

  6
   parameters of each zoning district, so long as it is consistent with overall community
  character.

  Two and three level buildings are permitted within the MD-R zoning district, depending
  on the average slope of the lot. Per AMC Section 9-5.305.e.1.i, on lots with an average
  slope of 14° or less, no portion of the building may exceed a height greater than 28 feet
  above the lot's natural surface and shall not be more than two levels. Lots with a steeper
  grade may increase up to three levels. Buildings within Sol Vista Condominiums vary
  between two and three stories depending on previous improvements made to each unit and
  the relationship to adjacent grade.

  Construction of the proposed lower-level family room and bathroom beneath the project
  site would result in the unit becoming three stories in height, which is not permitted because
  the average slope of the lot is approximately 10°. However, the proposed project meets all
  other development standards for a three-level building in the MD-R zone, including height
  and floor area. Therefore, it will comply with existing height and massing standards and
  will remain visually compatible with the surrounding Sol Vista Condominium community.

  Other units within the greater Sol Vista Condominium community have previously been
  granted approval for lower level, third story buildouts by the City, including 87 Sol Vista
  within the same building. Therefore, strict application of the development standard related
  to average lot slope and number of levels would deprive the property owner of the
  opportunity to expand the size of their unit in the same manner as other units within the
  same community.

2. Any variance granted shall be subject to such conditions as will assure that the
  adjustment thereby authorized shall not constitute a grant of special privileges
  inconsistent with the limitations upon other properties in the vicinity and zone in
  which such property is situated.

  Other units within the greater Sol Vista Condominium community have previously been
  granted approval for lower level, third story buildouts by the City, including 87 Sol Vista
  within the same building. Therefore, approval of the variance would not grant the applicant
  any special privileges inconsistent with existing property development patterns. Condition
  #6 of the draft Planning Commission resolution states that no conversion of the family
  room space to create a new bedroom shall be permitted without appropriate review by the
  Planning & Building Department and provision of a will serve letter from Southern
  California Edison Company (“SCE”) that adequate freshwater allocation is available for
  the proposed conversion.

3. A variance shall not be granted for a parcel of property which authorizes a use or
  activity which is not otherwise expressly authorized by the zone regulation governing
  the parcel of property.

  Attached single-family residential and congregate housing developments are conditionally
  permitted uses within the MD-R zoning district. The Sol Vista Condominium community was

  7
   developed as a congregate housing development and the proposed project will not change the
  use of the property or the overall character of the community, which consists of single-family
  and density bonus units.

4. No variances shall be granted which reduce or adversely affect access to or along the
  shoreline, including physical or visual qualities of access.

  The project site is located within an existing townhouse residential development that is not
  adjacent to, nor provides direct or indirect visual of physical access to, the shoreline of Avalon
  Bay or Lovers Cove to the north of the project site.

5.  The variance shall be consistent with the Local Coastal Program.

  The proposed project implements the following General Plan and Local Coastal Program
  Goals and Policies:

  Policy II-1 of the Land Use Element:

  “Use the City’s Zoning Ordinance and any applicable residential, commercial, resort,
  and open space design standards to guide the character of development and ensure
  compatibility with existing residential, commercial, resort, and open space uses.”

  The proposed project involves construction of a new family room and bathroom within
  the existing footprint of the residence, creating a new lower-level third story. The
  proposed project meets all other development standards for a three-level building in the
  MD-R zone, including height and floor area. Other units within the greater Sol Vista
  Condominium community have previously been granted approval for lower level, third
  story buildouts by the City, including 87 Sol Vista within the same building. Therefore,
  it will comply with existing height and massing standards and will remain visually
  compatible with the surrounding Sol Vista Condominium community.

  Policy II-3 of the Land Use Element:

  “Incorporate the policies of the Coastal Act (Public Resources Code Section 30210
  through 30263) as guiding policies of City’s land use.”

  The proposed project complies with Section 30250 of the Costal Act, which states:

  “(a) New residential, commercial, or industrial development, except as otherwise
  provided in this division, shall be located within, contiguous with, or in close proximity
  to, existing developed areas able to accommodate it or, where such areas are not able
  to accommodate it, in other areas with adequate public services and where it will not
  have significant adverse effects, either individually or cumulatively, on coastal
  resources. In addition, land divisions, other than leases for agricultural uses, outside
